sentences.text: Researchers investigated mice infected with the LCMV Armstrong virus by performing single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing to track the development of hundreds of individual T cell clones over time.

The number of early central memory precursors within a clone predicted whether that clone would become dominant in the memory phase, and clones sharing identical T cell receptor sequences were more likely to develop into similar cell types than random chance would suggest, despite significant variation in how individual clones differentiated.

Specific patterns in the T cell receptor sequences were linked to faster cell growth and a stronger focus on immediate immune responses, according to the authors' conclusion that these sequence features influence differentiation outcomes in this animal model.
